title: NVIDIA Announces DSX Ready Qualification Program for Data Center Power and Cooling Hardware
gist: NVIDIA launched the DSX Ready qualification program, initially covering battery energy storage systems (BESS) and cooling distribution units (CDUs), to certify third-party power/cooling vendors as compatible with its DGX/DSX AI factory racks -- with LG Electronics, LiquidStack and Vertiv qualified for CDUs and Hitachi Energy, LG Energy Solution and Tesla qualified for BESS at launch, and more component categories expected to follow.

themes.theme: DSX Ready program mechanics and intent

insights.claim: NVIDIA launched the DSX Ready qualification program to certify third-party battery energy storage systems (BESS) and cooling distribution units (CDUs) as compatible with its DSX AI factory racks -- two hardware classes NVIDIA itself does not manufacture.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: NVIDIA is extending its certification/branding leverage into adjacent power and cooling supply chains it doesn't directly sell into, creating a new gatekeeping layer for AI data center infrastructure vendors.
insights.quote: NVIDIA this week has announced that they are launching a new qualification program for DSX AI factory power and cooling parts.

insights.claim: NVIDIA explicitly signaled that batteries and cooling are only the starting categories and that it expects to expand DSX Ready to additional data center component types over time.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Investors should watch for DSX Ready to broaden into other power/rack infrastructure categories (e.g. PDUs, transformers, switchgear), expanding the set of vendors subject to NVIDIA certification and branding fees/requirements.
insights.quote: NVIDIA has also strongly hinted that CDUs and BESSes will not be the only data center components eventually covered by the program, taking care to note that this week’s announcement was for the “initial” categories of parts.

insights.claim: The program builds on NVIDIA's existing 'NVIDIA product qualified' label for CDUs, expanding both the scope of requirements and the range of component types covered.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: This is an incremental escalation of an existing certification scheme rather than a brand-new initiative, suggesting NVIDIA has been building toward broader hardware-ecosystem control for some time.

insights.claim: NVIDIA's stated goal with DSX Ready is to make DGX/DSX rack installation more turn-key, both by working with OEM partners to supply racks of critical hardware under the DGX AI factory blueprint and by giving customers clear guidance on which ancillary parts are confirmed compatible.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: A turn-key positioning strategy reduces integration risk for AI factory buyers and increases NVIDIA's influence over the full rack bill-of-materials, not just compute silicon.
insights.locator: The ultimate goal being to move the installation of DGX server racks

themes.theme: Differentiated qualification process by component complexity

insights.claim: CDU vendors under DSX Ready are allowed to self-qualify by meeting NVIDIA's published function and performance specifications, though NVIDIA still retains final sign-off authority.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: A lighter-touch self-certification path for cooling vendors likely means faster time-to-market and lower compliance cost for CDU suppliers versus battery/power suppliers.
insights.quote: CDU vendors are allowed to self-qualify based on meeting NVIDIA’s function and performance specifications (though they still need NVIDIA’s final approval).
insights.locator: Notably, the DSX Ready qualification process varies

insights.claim: BESS vendors face a more involved qualification process than CDU vendors, required to run their own qualification tests and submit the resulting data to NVIDIA for review and formal sign-off, which the author attributes to the greater complexity and tighter requirements of electrical work.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Higher qualification barriers for battery/power vendors could favor incumbent, well-resourced electrical equipment makers (e.g. Hitachi Energy, Tesla) over smaller BESS entrants trying to break into the AI data center supply chain.
insights.quote: BESS vendors, on the other hand, face a more involved process that requires running qualification tests and then submitting data to NVIDIA for them to review and sign off on – presumably owing to the more complex nature of electrical work and the tighter requirements thereof.
insights.locator: Notably, the DSX Ready qualification process varies

insights.claim: NVIDIA has not disclosed whether it charges vendors anything to participate in the DSX Ready program and use its branding.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Undisclosed monetization terms leave open whether DSX Ready becomes a direct revenue stream (licensing/certification fees) for NVIDIA beyond its hardware/software sales -- worth tracking in future disclosures or vendor commentary.
insights.quote: Meanwhile, the company is not disclosing what (if anything) it is charging for participating in the DSX Ready ecosystem and using the branding.
insights.locator: Notably, the DSX Ready qualification process varies

insights.claim: At launch, the first qualified CDU (cooling distribution unit) vendors under DSX Ready are LG Electronics, LiquidStack and Vertiv.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: These three cooling vendors gain an early NVIDIA-endorsed credential that could steer AI data center CDU procurement toward them ahead of competitors.
insights.quote: For the launch of the program, LG Electronics, LiquidStack and Vertiv are the first qualified CDU vendors.
insights.locator: For the launch of the program

insights.claim: At launch, the first qualified BESS (battery energy storage system) vendors under DSX Ready are Hitachi Energy, LG Energy Solution and Tesla.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Tesla, Hitachi Energy and LG Energy Solution now hold an NVIDIA-blessed credential for supplying battery backup into AI factory builds, positioning them ahead of un-qualified BESS suppliers in NVIDIA-centric data center deals.
insights.quote: Meanwhile Hitachi Energy, LG Energy Solution and Tesla are the first qualified BESS vendors.
insights.locator: For the launch of the program

insights.claim: DSX Ready is described as the latest in a long series of NVIDIA ecosystem plays around its data center business, joining existing ecosystems such as the CUDA software stack, the MGX modular server design platform, the NVLink cache-coherent network fabric ecosystem, and the broader DSX rack-scale systems ecosystem.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: NVIDIA's moat-building extends well beyond GPUs into software (CUDA), server design (MGX), interconnect (NVLink), and now power/cooling qualification (DSX Ready) -- a recurring pattern of NVIDIA embedding itself as the certifying/standard-setting layer across the full AI data center stack, which investors should read as sustained platform lock-in rather than a one-off announcement.
insights.quote: The DSX Ready program marks the latest in a long list of ecosystem plays from NVIDIA in and around the data center business.
